topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the fifth lecture of the Cancer Biology series, outlining the core themes of cancer evolution, cell of origin, and the microenvironment along with the intended learning outcomes.

topics.label: Genetic and epigenetic mechanisms in clonal selection and tumor development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how clonal fitness advantages from accumulated genetic mutations and non-mutational epigenetic alterations drive cancer initiation and Darwinian evolutionary selection.

topics.label: Cell of origin, stemness, and cancer stem cell models
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the relationship between normal tissue hierarchies and tumorigenesis, presenting experimental evidence for stem-like properties and cell-of-origin dynamics in leukemia and intestinal cancers.

topics.label: Microenvironmental influences on tumorigenesis, cellular interaction profiling, and evolutionary synthesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics demonstrate how inflammatory microenvironments and paracrine signals promote tumor initiation and maintenance, describe spatial technologies for profiling these cellular interactions, and synthesize the collective evolutionary model of cancer.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and upcoming topic
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the session and previews the upcoming lecture on cancer therapy.
